requirements.title: Fork tests against real deployed dependencies

evidence.description: Swapr Algebra NFPM smoke test proves real zero-liquidity fee materialization preserves position liquidity and NFT identity, drains fees before principal removal, and also covers full-unwind spot and source-activated fresh-pool conditional public-vault gas checks.

Real direct-Algebra removal proves zero-liquidity fee realization preserves liquidity and drains fees before an immediate principal removal, fee-bearing partial removal at 116,245 gas under a 150,000-gas bound, final removal, pair isolation, donation accounting, and the mutable-cooldown liveness failure.

Real Uniswap V3 integration exercises adapter-owned fresh pool creation, initialization, and first-NFT mint; proves zero-liquidity live-fee materialization preserves liquidity and NFT identity and drains fees before an immediate principal removal; and rejects reuse of the initialized pool.
Real futarchy proposal, Reality question, and CTF condition wiring fork test.
Futarchy conditional router split behavior fork test.
Shared Algebra stability guard resolves and checks the live GNO/sDAI spot pool over its 30-minute window.
Fork tests are documented as a required final target-address check.

remaining: Run the fork test suite against the selected final target proposal and token addresses before limited-funds execution.

requirements.title: Invariant and fuzz coverage for accounting and safety properties

evidence.description: Core manager tests cover every independent base/YES/NO token-ordering parity, proportional principal/fee/idle accounting with adversarial receipt-label misclassification, exact two-phase adapter-removal deltas with spot and conditional overreport rollback, divergent YES/NO liquidity and post-swap principal composition, sequential six-token conservation and nondecreasing survivor value per share, exact settlement after randomized one-to-four partial exits, donation-resistant deposit pricing, spot and conditional six-token post-exit fee/donation ownership, second-pool activation rollback, conditional underpayment fallback, exact-delta merge/winner/loser settlement rollback, and non-custodial emergency exit.
The production router test proves exact CTF split receipts and exact wrapper mint deltas.
The official proposal source test proves that every captured activation field must match the validated snapshot and that a corrupt capture rolls back both source and target state.

The real source-manager-router binding test proves first-conditional-add, canonical fresh-pool identity, second-CTF-split, second-fresh-position, and external post-activation resolver-binding rollback across coordinator state, registry, spot position, manager binding, wrappers, and fresh pools; and exact-replay or second-live-proposal rejection without changing active positions or binding.
Adapter over-pull safety test.

Deterministic Uniswap V3 adapter tests separate fee-only, partial-principal, and final-principal removal fields exactly; cover fresh create-initialize-first-mint ownership; reject uninitialized and initialized guarded/manipulated-price pre-existing pools before custody changes; and prove distinct pool-creation, initialization, and first-mint failures roll back pool creation, initialization, balances, and approvals.
Algebra guard tests cover inclusive 50-tick boundaries, signed TWAP rounding, and fail-closed history reads.

The initialized invariant harness interleaves deposits, activation, fees, donations, redemptions, and CTF settlement; every successful deposit and redemption checks survivor-favoring liquidity and six-token balance ratios, while global invariants enforce conditional binding, adapter-liquidity consistency, known custody of all six issued tokens, and zero managed residue at zero share supply.
Deeper invariant pass command is documented for pre-deploy review.

remaining: Run the deeper invariant pass documented in docs/readiness.md before mainnet-value deployment.
